reading.body:
This record is a single OpenStreetMap node in Italy tagged as a data center, with no confirmed operator, no website, and no power figure.

The only substantive fact is the tag itself. The name iZOOM.it follows a common Italian naming pattern for web-hosting and domain-registration businesses, which makes a small hosting or IT services operation plausible. The location, near Parma in northern Italy, is consistent with that reading but does not establish it.

For AI specifically, this tells us nothing about capacity. The record carries no megawatts, no operator, and no confirmation that a data center exists at these coordinates. A hosting business of this kind would sit far below the scale at which compute, buildings, and grid power become the binding constraints on AI training.

What the data does not cover is the important part. The research status is exhausted, meaning the entry was filed on the strength of a map tag and a plausible name rather than a verified source. It should be read as an unconfirmed candidate for a small Italian hosting site, not as evidence about Italy's data center footprint or its role in AI infrastructure.
